title: Where does an archetype's example content come from, and which settings must an author supply?
description: ST-DECL-UC01-R01 and R04 say each archetype supplies the smallest example content that checking accepts, and R05 says an empty scaffold names every setting the author must supply. Today the scaffolds of rpc-service and browser-service are refused: rpc-service needs the grpc-processes settings processes and proto_files, a proto file and a process factory package (factory/rpc.go) that imports the generated packages by the module path; browser-service needs a distinct api_prefix. The Archetype entity (ST-SUP-EN03) has no field that holds example content, and a component schema marks as required both settings the declaration must give and settings that only the running service gets (such as connection_string of postgres-adapter and issuer of jwt-auth), so checking cannot tell which settings an author must supply. Options: (a) add to the Archetype an example content field (files under the archetype folder and the settings to write into the declaration, with the module path as a placeholder), and mark in a component schema each setting the declaration must give, so that checking refuses its absence and init can name it; (b) keep the example content in Declaring's code, one case per archetype; (c) narrow R01, R04 and R05 to archetypes that can be empty, such as rest-crud. Recommendation: (a), since the UC01 notes say the archetype supplies its example content, and a registry change then needs no change to STEGO's code. Until then UC01-R01, R04-T01, R05 and the flow test stay not automated; rest-crud, which can be empty, already passes as written.

title: Which step of Record what a service was built from fulfills that apply writes the record inside the service's repo?
description: ST-GEN-UC01-R05 says that apply MUST write the record inside the service's repo, beside the code it generated. Only the step ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S02 (the service author commits the record with the generated code) fulfills it, and that step invokes no command, so no technical record can build the requirement, although ST-GEN-UC01-R05-T01 is automated and passes. Options: (a) ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S01, which invokes Apply a plan (ST-GEN-CMD01), also fulfills ST-GEN-UC01-R05, and S02 keeps it too; (b) S02 also invokes Apply a plan; (c) the requirement stays proved and not built. Recommendation: (a), since apply is what writes the record in the repo and the commit only shows it.

title: Which component puts the tenant column into the generated tables, their primary keys and their indexes, and which store takes the Tenant?
description: ST-SUP-RC27-OC03 says that the tenancy migration puts tenant_id as the leading column of the primary key and of every index of each tenant-owned table, and ST-SUP-RC27-OC01 says that every store method takes a Tenant. But the PostgreSQL adapter (ST-SUP-RC01) makes the entity tables with GORM AutoMigrate, with the primary key id and no tenant column, and its store methods take no tenant. The command and query capabilities (ST-SUP-RC32, ST-SUP-RC33) need the same column for PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, id) (ST-SUP-RP06-LC22). Also, ST-DECL-EN09 lets tenancy.key name the field, such as org_id, but OC03 names the column tenant_id. Options: (a) when tenancy is pooled, RC01 emits the tenant column as the leading column of the primary key and of each index of each owned table, and its store methods take tenant.Tenant and open each transaction through tenant.Begin; RC27 emits only row-level security, the policies, the roles, the role grants and the tenant list migration; (b) RC27 emits a migration after the initial migration of RC01 that adds the column and makes the primary key and every index again, as ST-SUP-RC29-OC06 adds authz_token; (c) the runtime-based store of RC32 and RC33 takes the place of the GORM store for a service with tenancy, and that store emits the column. For the name: (1) the column is always tenant_id, and tenancy.key names only the claim field; (2) the column has the name of tenancy.key, and OC03 reads tenant_id as that key. Recommendation: (a) with (1), because the table and its keys have one owner, a later rebuild of keys on a full table takes long locks (ST-SUP-RC01-OC39), and the runtime, the outbox and the audit table all use tenant_id. Until this is decided, the tenancy builder cannot build OC01, OC03, OC04, OC07 and OC08.

title: Is a tenant-less worker with runs_as system a declared exception, or does every worker and controller iterate tenants?
description: ST-SUP-RC27-OC06 and its four tests need a cleanup worker declared with tenants none, runs_as system and a reason, which reaches a tenant-less path through a distinct bypass role. But ST-DECL-INV20 says that a controller MUST declare tenants each and that checking MUST refuse tenants none; the worker of ST-DECL-EN25 has no tenants, runs_as or reason field; and the tenant runtime (ST-SUP-RP04) has no bypass-role connector, although ST-SUP-RC27-G01 says that it lives in the runtime library. So the declaration that the OC06 tests start from is refused today. Options: (a) retire OC06 and its tests, because INV20 forbids every tenant-less path; the tenant-less refusal is then proved by the declaration checks of INV20 alone; (b) add tenants, runs_as and reason to the worker and the controller, let INV20 admit tenants none only with runs_as system and a reason, and add a bypass-role connector, which logs each call, to the tenant runtime. Recommendation: (a), because INV20 is the later decision, a bypass role is a role that can read every tenant, which works against ST-BO06 (golden paths stay safe); a cleanup across tenants can run through tenant.EachListed, one transaction per tenant.
